work.summary:
I re-ran the audit's final forward Monte Carlo with every tax set to zero, keeping all other assumptions of the verified final run. The work is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-snt-2b-adam-cieniewicz/4246b01c-1857-5934-aed2-b3eb85d88a07/scratchpad/audit/cv_avant_impot/. It uses the same series.pkl, the same seed (20261005) and the same order of index generation, so the bootstrap shocks are identical: stationary bootstrap, mean block 126 days, 5,000 paths, horizons 5 and 10 years.

**Sanity check: exact match.** With the previous fixed costs (500/625/1,000), the new pre-tax medians, P10 and P90 for all 36 DIY rows equal the pre_med/pre_p10/pre_p90 of cv_rendement/final_table.csv. The largest gap is 1e-14 point. The UCITS trend ETF and 100 % equity rows also match exactly. There is no gap to explain: the old pre_med already came from sim_diy with pfu=0 on the same shocks.

**Two engine defects had to be fixed in my copy of mc_engine.py.** Setting the taxes to zero as the brief describes would not have removed all tax.
- (i) In sim_diy, sim_etf and sim_mix, P_below_cash always compared against the cash fund after a 31.4 % tax. I added a `cash_tax` argument and set it to 0, so the cash benchmark is now 2.30 %/yr (€STR 2.4 % minus 0.10 %).
- (ii) sim_mix taxed gains realised at the annual rebalance at a hard-coded 31.4 %, even with tax_e=tax_t=0. I added `reb_tax` and set it to 0.

**Mix check without the engine.** A direct recomputation of the 70/30 mix with no tax matches the engine to within 0.003 point. That remaining gap comes from reading the equity drift back from a rounded text label in the check script, not from the engine. A direct recomputation of the ETF matches exactly.

**Central results at 10 years, before tax, DIY fixed costs USD 400/yr.** Each figure is the median CAGR, with the 10th–90th percentile range in brackets.
- Cash: 2.30 %.
- DIY at 21 % vol: 100k 3.55 % [−4.9; 12.4]; 250k 4.85 % [−4.3; 14.3]; 1M 5.56 % [−3.9; 15.6].
- DIY at 12 % vol: 100k 2.21 % [−2.5; 7.1]; 250k 3.67 % [−1.1; 8.5]; 1M 4.69 % [−0.6; 10.1].
- UCITS trend ETF: 4.76 % [0.1; 9.7].
- 100 % S&P-type: 6.00 % [−1.7; 13.0]. This median is the calibration target, so it is set by assumption.
- 100 % Nasdaq-type: 6.00 % [−5.1; 15.5].
- 70/30 S&P/ETF: 6.08 % [1.1; 10.9].
- 70/30 Nasdaq/ETF: 6.30 % [−0.7; 12.6].

**Fixed costs.** Going from USD 150 to USD 1,000 a year moves the 10-year central DIY median by:
- 0.81 point at 100k and 21 % vol (3.78 % to 2.97 %);
- 0.85 point at 100k and 12 % vol (2.45 % to 1.60 %);
- 0.30 point at 250k (4.93 % to 4.63 %);
- 0.08 point at 1M (5.59 % to 5.51 %).

**Time cost.** Valuing 80 h × EUR 25 (about USD 2,340/yr) on top of USD 400 gives medians of 1.11 % at 100k/21 %, −0.31 % at 100k/12 %, 3.98 % at 250k/21 % and 5.37 % at 1M/21 %.

**MC noise.** I re-ran the central 10-year cases with 6 fresh seeds. The seed-to-seed standard deviation of the median is 0.06–0.15 point. The main seed is a favourable draw for DIY at 21 % vol: +0.27 point at 100k and +0.24 at 250k against the 6-seed mean, +0.09 at 1M, and +0.14 to +0.15 at 12 % vol for 100k and 250k. It is neutral for the ETF (−0.004) and for 70/30 (+0.035). So at 250k and 21 % vol, DIY (4.85 %, or 4.61 % on the 6-seed mean) and the ETF (4.76 %) cannot be told apart. At 1M, DIY at 21 % vol is about 0.7–0.8 point above the ETF before time cost.

**Column names.** In the new tables the at_* columns keep their old names so rapport_audit.py can read them, but here they are pre-tax (pre_* equals at_*). DIY rows carry two new columns, fixed_set and fixed_usd. Wealth is in USD-equivalent units, so the 100k tier means USD 100k.

**Internal only.** sanity_check_pre_med.csv also contains the old after-tax medians and a tax_drag_pt column, for the check alone. Under the user's request these must not go into the report.

facts.fact: With the previous fixed costs (USD 500/625/1,000), the new pre-tax DIY medians, P10 and P90 are bit-identical to pre_med/pre_p10/pre_p90 in cv_rendement/final_table.csv; the largest absolute gap is about 1e-14 point. The UCITS ETF and 100 % equity pre_med are also identical. The reason is the same seed, same order of index generation and same series, and the old pre-tax column was already computed with pfu=0.

The old engine always measured P_below_cash against the cash fund after 31.4 % tax (cash_benchmark default tax=PFU), even when pfu=0 or tax=0 was passed. The patched copy adds cash_tax, set to 0, so the cash benchmark is 2.30 %/yr.

sim_mix taxed gains realised at the annual rebalance at a hard-coded PFU (31.4 %), even with tax_e=tax_t=0. A reb_tax argument was added and set to 0. A direct recomputation without the engine confirms the 70/30 results to within 0.003 point (the gap comes only from parsing a rounded equity drift in the check script); the ETF matches exactly.

Forward Sharpe ±0.10 moves the 10y central median by about ±2.2–2.3 points for DIY at 21 % vol, about ±1.25 for DIY at 12 % vol, ±1.27 for the ETF and ±0.38 for 70/30. €STR ±0.5 % moves DIY at 21 % by about ±0.40 point, DIY at 12 % by about ±0.45, the ETF by ±0.53, 70/30 by ±0.15 and cash by ±0.50.

Adding 80 h × EUR 25 (about USD 2,340/yr) on top of the USD 400 budget gives 10y central medians of 1.11 % at 100k/21 % (P below cash 56.5 %), -0.31 % at 100k/12 %, 3.98 % at 250k/21 %, 2.81 % at 250k/12 %, 5.37 % at 1M/21 % and 4.49 % at 1M/12 %. At 100k, DIY is then below cash.

Across 6 fresh seeds (5,000 paths each), the standard deviation of the 10y central median is 0.06–0.15 point. The main seed sits above the 6-seed mean for DIY: +0.27 point (100k/21 %), +0.24 (250k/21 %), +0.09 (1M/21 %), +0.14 (100k/12 %), +0.15 (250k/12 %), +0.04 (1M/12 %). It is neutral for the ETF (-0.004) and 70/30 S&P (+0.035). The 6-seed mean DIY medians are 3.27 / 4.61 / 5.48 at 21 % and 2.07 / 3.52 / 4.65 at 12 % vol.

Before tax, DIY at 250k and 21 % vol (4.85 %, or 4.61 % on the 6-seed mean) cannot be told apart from the UCITS trend ETF (4.76 %), with nearly twice the drawdown (-46 % vs -25 % median; worst decile -66 % vs -36 %). DIY beats the ETF clearly only at 1M (about +0.7–0.8 point at 21 % vol) and only if time is not counted. DIY at 100k is below the ETF in all three fixed-cost budgets, and the 12 % vol version at 100k is roughly cash-like (2.21 % vs 2.30 %, P below cash 51 %). The 70/30 mixes give the best ratio of median to risk.

In final_table_avant_impot.csv the at_* columns keep their old names for rapport_audit.py compatibility but are pre-tax (pre_* equals at_*). DIY rows add fixed_set (ibg150, ibg400, ibg1000, prev_500_625_1000) and fixed_usd. Case names were renamed to remove account and tax wording: 'd EUR cash (XEON-type MMF, acc.)', 'e 100% equities (sp|nq)', 'e 70/30 annual rebalance (sp|nq)'. Wealth is in USD-equivalent units (100k tier = USD 100k). The equities' 6 % central median at 10 years is a calibration target, not a result.
sanity_check_pre_med.csv contains the old after-tax medians and a tax_drag_pt column for internal checking only; per the user's request these must not appear in the new PDF.

verification.summary:
**Verdict.** The pre-tax re-run is correct: no tax is left anywhere in the code path, and an independent re-implementation reproduces it. But the report should not use the main-seed DIY medians as they stand. That seed flatters DIY by about +0.25 point at 100k/250k and 21 % vol, which is enough to flip the "DIY 250k vs ETF" ordering. The generator also needs two code fixes before it can read the new table.

**Re-implementation.** In /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-snt-2b-adam-cieniewicz/4246b01c-1857-5934-aed2-b3eb85d88a07/scratchpad/audit/verif_avant_impot/indep.py I rewrote the stationary bootstrap index construction (vectorised, not the audit's loop), the DIY simulator, the fund, the 70/30 annual-rebalance mix, the summary statistics and the equity calibration. The file has no tax parameter at all.
- **Same shocks (run_same.py → compare_same_shocks.csv).** All 48 DIY cells checked match final_table_avant_impot.csv to under 1e-6 point. That covers median, P10, P90, P(loss), P(below cash), median and worst-decile drawdown, and P(touch 60 %). The UCITS ETF matches exactly. 100 % equities and the 70/30 mixes are within 0.0006 point; the gap is only that my bisection calibration hits exactly 6.000 % where theirs stops at 5.9998 %.
- **Previous pre_med.** The prev_500_625_1000 DIY rows, the ETF and equities equal cv_rendement/final_table.csv pre_med. The old table had no pre-tax value for 70/30 or cash. Those figures are new and are confirmed by my code and by their engine-free check.

**No tax left.** The two engine defects are real: the cash benchmark was always taxed at 31.4 %, and sim_mix had a hard-coded 31.4 % tax on rebalancing gains. Both are fixed in the copy. Every call passes pfu=0, tax=0, reb_tax=0 and cash_tax=0. The only exception is calib(), which keeps the default cash_tax but reads only pre_med, so it does not matter. P(below cash) matches my untaxed 2.30 % benchmark exactly.
- **Report generator (rapport_audit.py).** It still contains about 41 tax mentions and reads the old after-tax cv_rendement/final_table.csv. Three of its four old case names were renamed in the new table: cash, 100 % equities and 70/30. Those lookups will fail loudly.
- **Silent DIY trap.** row() and scen() have no fixed_set filter. Their .iloc[0] would silently return the ibg150 row: 3.78 % instead of 3.55 % at 100k. The generator must filter fixed_set=='ibg400', or read rendement_attendu_10ans_avant_impot.csv instead.
- **Strings not to print.** Avoid the 'PRE-TAX;' text in the assumptions column, the pre_tax_* column names, sanity_check_pre_med.csv, PEA/CTO/PFU wording, and "après/avant impôt". Prefer "rendements bruts", or say nothing about it.

**Seed robustness.** I ran 4 fresh seeds × 10,000 paths (run_fresh2.py, run_fresh3.py).
- **10y central medians.** DIY at 21 % vol: 3.27 / 4.60 / 5.41 (100k / 250k / 1M). DIY at 12 % vol: 2.08 / 3.52 / 4.64. ETF 4.69. S&P 5.99 and Nasdaq 5.93, with mu held at the calibrated values. 70/30 S&P 6.03. 70/30 Nasdaq 6.36.
- **Agreement with their seed-noise run.** Their 6-seed means for DIY are within 0.07 of mine. Pooling all 75k paths gives 3.29 / 4.62 / 5.45 at 21 % vol and 2.08 / 3.53 / 4.65 at 12 % vol, ETF 4.72, 70/30 S&P 6.04.
- **What is robust.** The fixed-cost and time-cost deltas are identical across seeds. Risk metrics move by at most about 1.3 point; fresh-seed P(loss) and P(below cash) for DIY are 0.2–1.3 point higher.

**Plausibility (Gaussian i.i.d. benchmark, same drift and vol).** DIY medians are within 0.03–0.16 point of the bootstrap. Median drawdowns agree within 1.3 points and P(touch 60 %) within 4 points. Analytically, 250k at 21 % vol gives log growth of 4.42 %, about 4.5 % CAGR, against a robust bootstrap median of 4.6 %. So 4.85 % is mostly seed luck.
- **Equities and 70/30.** Bootstrap risk is lower than Gaussian. For S&P, P(loss) is 15.6 % vs 18.7 %; for 70/30 S&P it is 5.7 % vs 9.4 %. This reflects equity mean reversion in the 2000–26 sample (10y effective vol is below daily vol) and trend behaviour in crises. It is sample-dependent and probably flattering for 70/30.
- **Calibration.** Holding the median at 6 % means the bootstrap's mean log growth is only about 5.5 % for S&P and 5.1 % for Nasdaq. That is acceptable but worth knowing.

**Interpretation, corrected.**
- At 250k and 21 % vol, DIY (about 4.6 %) is equal to or slightly below the ETF (about 4.7 %), with roughly twice its drawdown.
- At 1M, DIY at 21 % vol beats the ETF by about +0.7 point, before any time cost.
- At equal 12 % risk, DIY never beats the ETF in the central case (2.1 / 3.5 / 4.6 vs 4.7).
- At 100k and 12 % vol, the median is slightly below cash (2.1 vs 2.3 %; P(below cash) 52 %), not merely "cash-like".

**Out of my lens, for the costs job.**
- **Fixed-cost slope.** Each extra USD 1,000/yr of fixed cost costs about −1.05 point at 100k, −0.36 at 250k and −0.09 at 1M. A real-time ICE subscription (about $1.7–1.9k/yr) would sit above the tested range.
- **Execution lag.** It barely matters for the subsets: one extra day costs only 0.02–0.03 Sharpe (lag_check.csv). Automating through IB Gateway therefore needs no change to the Sharpe grid.
